name: Azmyth
appearance: A crested bat with a bearded chin, white pupil-less eyes, and leathery gray, mauve, or emerald green skin. Its tail ends in a needle-sharp point.

habitats: Solitary wanderers that return to favorite haunts

Physical attacks.name: Bite and tail stab
Physical attacks.effectNote: The bite deals 1 damage and the tail stab deals 1d2.

Magic.name: Invisibility
Magic.effectNote: Self only, once per day for up to six rounds. It ends when the Azmyth makes a successful attack.

Magic.name: Silence
Magic.effectNote: Once per day, centered on the Azmyth in a 15-foot radius.

Magic.name: Shocking grasp
Magic.effectNote: Twice per day, direct contact deals 1d8+6 electrical damage. It can be added to a physical attack.

Behavior.name: Voluntary companionship
Behavior.effectNote: Azmyths sometimes form lifelong partnerships with humanoids. The entry distinguishes them from familiars under a wizard’s direct control.

notes: Rare, solitary, and active at any time. Omnivore. High intelligence (13–14). Chaotic neutral. Elite (14) morale. Treasure Nil. 1 appearing.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, January 1994 third printing, pp. 15–16.

name: Night Hunter
appearance: A velvet-black bat, including its wing claws, with violet, orange, or red eyes and a sharp triangular tail.

habitats: Double-ended caves, the underworld, and tall dense woods
combat.attackOptions: One bite, two wing-claw rakes, and either a tail slash or a tail stab.

Physical attacks.name: Bite and wing claws
Physical attacks.effectNote: Bite for 1d4, and rake once with each wing claw for 1d2 per rake.

Physical attacks.name: Tail slash or stab
Physical attacks.effectNote: Choose a slash for 1d6 or a stab for 3d4.

Behavior.name: Ambush
Behavior.effectNote: It flies low and uses terrain as cover. Its loud calls when excited make surprise uncommon.

Behavior.name: Lair counts
Behavior.effectNote: The table gives 1–12 appearing and 1–30 in a lair. The prose says lairs usually hold over 30.

notes: Also called dragazhar. Uncommon pack hunter. Nocturnal above ground and active at any time underground. Carnivore. Average to high intelligence (8–14). Neutral evil. Steady (11) morale. Treasure M, O, Z in lair. The table lists no special attacks, special defenses, or magic resistance.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, January 1994 third printing, pp. 15–16.

name: Sinister
appearance: A jet-black, manta ray-shaped bat with no distinct head or neck. Its muscular wings lack the conspicuous finger bones of other bats.

habitats: Above-ground hunting grounds used mostly at night
languages: Telepathy 20 ft., only with other Sinisters

Magic.name: Levitation
Magic.effectNote: Natural precision levitation lets it hang motionless.

Magic.name: Energy field
Magic.effectNote: A naturally generated, five-foot-deep field surrounds it at all times. The field repels ordinary missiles and absorbs missile spells such as magic missile and Melf’s acid arrow. Melee attacks and other spells are unaffected by the field.

Magic.name: Hold monster
Magic.effectNote: Once per day. Usually saved for escape, though it may use the spell when hunting.

Behavior.name: Music
Behavior.effectNote: Silent bands may gather around singers or musicians and follow them. The prose says they leave performers alone unless attacked.

Behavior.name: Alignment discrepancy
Behavior.effectNote: The table gives lawful evil. The prose describes Sinisters as non-evil.

notes: Rare, found in bands of 1d6, and active at any time. Omnivore. Average to exceptional intelligence (8–16). Champion (15–16) morale. Treasure Nil.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, January 1994 third printing, pp. 15–16.
